summary: 59-year-old man, sudden generalised peritonitis after 3 days of LIF pain, T 38.7 °C, HR 116, BP 118/70; CT: free gas and generalised fluid, no faecal contamination.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Severe generalised abdominal pain and fever
inputs.hpi: 3 days of left lower abdominal pain; this morning sudden worsening with pain across the whole abdomen, fever and vomiting. Known diverticular disease.

exam.abdomen: Generalised peritonism: guarding and rigidity throughout, maximal in the left iliac fossa. Bowel sounds absent.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Perforated sigmoid diverticulitis with free intraperitoneal gas and generalised free fluid; no faecal contamination seen.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Perforated diverticulitis with purulent peritonitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Perforated sigmoid diverticulitis with generalised purulent peritonitis (Hinchey III). Emergency surgery: sigmoid resection with primary anastomosis ± defunctioning stoma, or Hartmann's procedure.

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: iOS: ClinicalPathwayEngine reads only CC/PMH keywords; CC 'Severe generalised abdominal pain and fever' gives 'routine'.

mustInclude.note: The documented plan must contain the emergency operation for Hinchey III.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Word-boundary Hinchey matching and specific-first variant order (peritonitis before abscess).

mustInclude.note: WSES 2020: in stable, immunocompetent patients, resection with primary anastomosis ± diverting stoma is an alternative to Hartmann's.

guideline.name: WSES guidelines — acute colonic diverticulitis in the emergency setting (2020 update)
guideline.section: CT staging (WSES CT classification); uncomplicated: antibiotics not always needed in immunocompetent patients, outpatient care; abscess >4–5 cm: percutaneous drainage + antibiotics; generalised peritonitis: emergency surgery (Hartmann's or resection with primary anastomosis ± stoma); immunocompromised: high risk, antibiotics, low threshold for surgery
guideline.citation: Sartelli M, Weber DG, Kluger Y, et al. 2020 update of the WSES guidelines for the management of acute colonic diverticulitis in the emergency setting. World J Emerg Surg. 2020;15:32.

guideline.name: AGA clinical practice update — medical management of colonic diverticulitis
guideline.section: Antibiotics used selectively rather than routinely in immunocompetent patients with mild uncomplicated diverticulitis; CT when diagnosis uncertain; colonoscopy after complicated diverticulitis or if not recently done
guideline.citation: Peery AF, Shaukat A, Strate LL. AGA clinical practice update on medical management of colonic diverticulitis: expert review. Gastroenterology. 2021;160:906–11.e1.

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — left-sided colonic diverticulitis
guideline.section: Selective antibiotics for uncomplicated disease; percutaneous drainage for large abscess; urgent colectomy for diffuse peritonitis; immunocompromised patients; colonoscopy after complicated disease
guideline.citation: Hall J, Hardiman K, Lee S, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of left-sided colonic diverticulitis. Dis Colon Rectum. 2020;63:728–47.

guideline.name: Modified Hinchey classification
guideline.section: 0 mild; Ia confined pericolic inflammation/phlegmon; Ib pericolic or mesocolic abscess; II pelvic/distant abscess; III generalised purulent peritonitis; IV faecal peritonitis
guideline.citation: Wasvary H, Turfah F, Kadro O, Beauregard W. Same hospitalization resection for acute diverticulitis. Am Surg. 1999;65:632–5.

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign — international guidelines for sepsis and septic shock 2021
guideline.section: Screening (do not use qSOFA alone), antibiotics within 1 h of shock, blood cultures, lactate, 30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypoperfusion, vasopressors, source control
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2021. Crit Care Med. 2021;49:e1063–e1143.

rationale: Permutation: Hinchey III. Emergency surgery (primary anastomosis ± stoma in a stable patient, or Hartmann's) with antibiotics; the documented plan must follow the Hinchey grade in the assessment.
